_meta.purpose: Authoritative REALISTIC serving-size reference so a generated meal plan never shows weird portions (no '2.25 slices of bread', '5 tortillas for 1.5 oz turkey', '2 berries = 120 g'). For each food category: the normal human serving (household unit + grams), the realistic min/max a coach would actually plate, whether the food comes in WHOLE COUNTABLE units (snap to integers) or is SCOOPABLE/weighable (snap to clean grams), and the typical grams-per-unit.
how_to_use: When the planner picks grams for a food, snap to this reference instead of emitting raw decimals.
countable=true  -> round the household quantity to a whole number of units (1, 2, 3 eggs/slices/tortillas), then grams = units * grams_per_unit. Never plate 2.25 slices or 0.4 eggs.
countable=false -> snap grams to the food's scoop_step (e.g. 5 g for oils/nut butter, 10 g for most foods, 25 g for cooked grains/proteins) and keep within [min_g, max_g].
If the macro target needs more than max_g of one food, add a second food rather than plating an absurd single portion (the 'don't make someone eat 5 tortillas' rule).
serving_g is the DEFAULT 'one normal serving' to seed a portion before macro-fitting. min_g / max_g are the realistic plating bounds a coach would accept.
primary_sources: FDA Reference Amounts Customarily Consumed (RACC), 21 CFR 101.12(b) - the federal legal definition of one normal eating-occasion serving. Anchor for serving_g.
USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy / FNDDS) food_portion gram weights - anchor for grams_per_unit of countable items and cup/tbsp weights.
British Dietetic Association (BDA) Food Fact Sheet 'Portion Sizes' - dietitian-facing plating portions with household + handful measures. Anchor for realistic coach min/max.
USDA FDA grading standard: USDA Large egg = 50 g (shelled); medium 44 g, extra-large 56 g.

conventions.weighing_state: All gram values are the EDIBLE PORTION in the state the food is normally weighed for a plan: proteins/grains/legumes COOKED; veg/fruit RAW unless noted; fats/oils/nut-butter/condiments as-is. Matches the cooked/raw 'form' flag already on each food in foods.js.
conventions.countable_meaning: true = food is eaten as discrete whole pieces (egg, bread slice, tortilla, string cheese, medium fruit). Quantity must round to whole units. false = scoopable/poured/weighable (rice, oil, yogurt, ground meat) - snap grams instead.
conventions.scoop_step_g: Smallest gram increment to snap a non-countable food to, so portions read clean (e.g. 120 g not 117.3 g).

proteins_meat_poultry.min_household: 3 oz / deck of cards (RACC + 'deck of cards' rule)
proteins_meat_poultry.notes: RACC for a meat main = 85 g (3 oz) no-sauce, 140 g (5 oz) with sauce. BDA plates 90 g. Coaches commonly run 113-170 g cooked for fat-loss protein targets. Above ~227 g cooked in one sitting reads as unrealistic for one person - split across meals.
proteins_meat_poultry.source: FDA RACC 85 g/140 g; BDA 90 g (deck of cards); USDA cooked-meat 100 g reference.

proteins_fish_seafood.notes: BDA plates fish at 140 g (palm of hand) for both white and oily fish - larger than the 85 g meat RACC because fish is leaner/less dense. A standard salmon fillet runs 113-170 g cooked. Canned tuna: 1 drained 5 oz can = ~120 g drained, snap to that.
proteins_fish_seafood.source: BDA 140 g (palm); FDA RACC fish 85 g no-sauce.

eggs.notes: ALWAYS round to whole eggs - never plate 1.4 eggs. USDA grading: large = 50 g shelled, medium 44 g, extra-large 56 g, jumbo 63 g. One large egg WHITE = ~33 g. RACC = 50 g (1 large). Normal breakfast = 2-3 whole eggs; add egg whites (countable, 33 g each) to push protein without more yolk fat.
eggs.source: USDA/FDA egg grade standard (large = 50 g); FDA RACC eggs 50 g.

tofu_plant_protein.max_household: 1 full block (about 1/2 a 14 oz package per person ceiling)
tofu_plant_protein.notes: A standard US firm-tofu block = 396-454 g (14-16 oz). Plate in clean fractions of a block: 1/4 block ~100 g, 1/2 block ~200 g. RACC for tofu = 85 g. Tempeh is denser - serving 85-113 g.
tofu_plant_protein.source: FDA RACC tofu 85 g; standard 14 oz block.

grains_rice_quinoa_pasta_cooked.notes: RACC for cooked rice/pasta = 140 g (~1 cup). BDA plates 150 g cooked. Snap to clean half-cup steps: 1/2 cup, 3/4 cup, 1 cup, 1.5 cups. Never plate '0.65 cup'. Cooked-grain cup weights differ by grain (rice ~158 g, quinoa 185 g, pasta 140 g) - use cup_weights_g, not a single number.
grains_rice_quinoa_pasta_cooked.source: FDA RACC 140 g; BDA 150 g; USDA FoodData Central cooked-grain cup weights.

grains_oats_dry.notes: Oats are almost always weighed DRY in a plan. 1/2 cup dry rolled oats = ~40 g (the label serving). RACC for cereal = 40 g. Don't confuse dry vs cooked: 40 g dry oats becomes ~1 cup cooked. Plate 30-60 g dry for most; 80 g dry is a very large bowl.
grains_oats_dry.source: FDA RACC cereal 40 g; oat label serving 40 g (1/2 cup dry).

grains_bread.notes: ALWAYS round to whole slices - never plate 2.25 slices. Standard sandwich slice = 28-36 g (use 32 g; thick/artisan slices 40-45 g, thin sandwich slices 25 g). RACC = 50 g (1-2 slices). A sandwich = 2 slices; toast = 1-2 slices. Bagel is a separate item (~95-110 g each, also countable).
grains_bread.source: FDA RACC bread 50 g (1-2 slices); BDA 34-36 g/slice; USDA white-bread slice 25-28 g.

grains_tortilla.serving_household: 2 medium flour tortillas (taco) OR 1 large burrito
grains_tortilla.notes: ALWAYS round to whole tortillas. NEVER do the '5 tortillas for 1.5 oz turkey' footgun - if a wrap needs more filling, add filling, not tortillas. Sizes: corn (6 in) ~28 g, flour fajita/taco (8 in) ~45 g, flour burrito (10-12 in) ~72 g. Tacos = 2-3 small; burrito = 1 large.
grains_tortilla.source: USDA: flour tortilla 45 g medium / 72 g burrito; corn tortilla 28 g.

grains_potato.notes: Potatoes are semi-countable: a medium potato = ~173 g cooked, but coaches often weigh them, so allow gram-snapping between sizes too. BDA plates 175 g (3 egg-sized). Sweet potato medium = ~130 g. Don't plate '1.4 potatoes' - either round to whole potatoes or state grams ('about 200 g').
grains_potato.source: USDA medium potato 173 g; BDA 175 g; FDA RACC potato (fresh) 110 g.

legumes_beans_lentils_cooked.notes: RACC for beans = 130 g (~1 cup, in-sauce/canned). BDA plates 150 g (4 tbsp). Snap to half-cup steps. Cooked legume cup weights: lentils 198 g, black beans 172 g, chickpeas 164 g. Beans-as-side ~1/2 cup; beans-as-main (chili, dal) up to 1 cup.
legumes_beans_lentils_cooked.source: FDA RACC beans 130 g; BDA 150 g; USDA cooked-legume cup weights.

vegetables.max_household: 2-3 cups (free-volume veg, no real ceiling for fat-loss)

countable_veg._note: A few veg ARE countable - round these to whole pieces

vegetables.notes: RACC = 85 g (~1 cup) cooked/frozen veg; raw leafy = 85 g but only ~30 g/cup so it's 3 cups. BDA plates 80 g (3 heaped tbsp). Most non-starchy veg are 'free volume' for fat-loss - max_g is generous (2-3 cups). A medium tomato/pepper/carrot is countable; loose chopped veg is scoopable.
vegetables.source: FDA RACC veg 85 g; BDA 80 g; USDA cup weights (leafy ~30 g, cooked non-leafy ~90 g).

fruit.serving_household: 1 medium piece OR about 1 cup berries
fruit.notes: CRITICAL footgun rule: berries are SCOOPABLE BY CUP, not countable by berry - never write '2 berries = 120 g' (that's ~10 berries). Whole tree/vine fruit IS countable: round apples/bananas/oranges to whole pieces (1 medium banana = 118 g, never 0.7 banana). RACC = 140 g. Cut fruit / berries: snap grams to a clean fraction of a cup (1/2 cup ~75 g, 1 cup ~150 g). BDA portion = 80 g.
fruit.source: FDA RACC fruit 140 g; BDA 80 g; USDA medium-fruit weights (apple 182 g, banana 118 g, orange 131 g) + berry cup weights.

fats_oils.notes: RACC for fats/oils = 1 tbsp (14 g). Snap to tsp/tbsp multiples: 5 g (~1 tsp), 9 g (2 tsp), 14 g (1 tbsp). Oil is calorie-dense - a realistic 'cooking the meal' amount is 1 tsp-1 tbsp; >2 tbsp (28 g = 250 kcal) on one plate is almost always a planner error. BDA spread/oil portion = 5 g (1 tsp).
fats_oils.source: FDA RACC oil 1 tbsp/14 g; BDA 5 g; USDA 1 tbsp oil = 13.5-14 g.

nuts_seeds.notes: RACC for nuts/seeds = 30 g (1 oz, ~2 tbsp). BDA = 30 g (one handful). Snap to 5 g steps. Nuts are calorie-dense (1 oz almonds ~160 kcal) - a realistic plate is 1/2 to 1.5 oz; rarely above 42 g. Chia/flax used as 1-2 tbsp (12-24 g) toppers, not handfuls.
nuts_seeds.source: FDA RACC nuts 30 g; BDA 30 g (handful); USDA 1 oz = 28 g.

nut_butter.notes: RACC for nut butter = 2 tbsp (32 g). 1 tbsp peanut butter = ~16 g. Snap to ~16 g (1 tbsp) steps. Calorie-dense (2 tbsp PB ~190 kcal) - realistic plate is 1-2 tbsp; 3 tbsp is the ceiling. BDA = 30 g (1 tbsp by their measure). PBfit powder is much lighter per tbsp (~6 g powder) - treat by powder grams, not PB grams.
nut_butter.source: FDA RACC nut butter 2 tbsp/32 g; BDA 30 g; USDA 1 tbsp PB = 16 g.

dairy_yogurt.notes: RACC for yogurt = 170 g (the standard single-serve pot). BDA = 125-150 g (one pot). Snap to 10 g steps. Greek yogurt is the protein workhorse - realistic plate 150-250 g; a 1-cup (245 g) bowl is the upper end. Don't plate odd numbers like 187 g - snap to 150/170/200/250.
dairy_yogurt.source: FDA RACC yogurt 170 g; BDA 125-150 g; USDA 1 cup yogurt = 245 g.

dairy_milk.notes: RACC for milk = 240 mL/g (1 cup). Snap to clean fractions of a cup (1/4, 1/2, 1 cup). Plant milks ~the same volume but lighter (~1 cup almond milk = 240 g but ~30-40 kcal). A 'splash' in oats/coffee = 1/4-1/2 cup; a glass = 1 cup.
dairy_milk.source: FDA RACC milk 240 mL; USDA 1 cup milk = 244 g.

dairy_cottage_ricotta.notes: RACC for cottage cheese = 110 g (1/2 cup). Snap to half-cup steps. High-protein, low-cal - a protein-forward plate runs 1/2 to 1 cup (113-226 g). Ricotta is denser/fattier - use as a 50-100 g topping, not a 1-cup serving.
dairy_cottage_ricotta.source: FDA RACC cottage cheese 110 g (1/2 cup); USDA 1 cup = 226 g.

dairy_cheese_hard.notes: RACC for hard cheese = 30 g (1 oz). BDA = 30 g (matchbox). Cheese is dual-mode: a STRING-CHEESE stick (28 g) or a deli SLICE (19 g) is countable - round to whole sticks/slices. Shredded/crumbled/grated is scoopable - snap grams (1/4 cup shredded ~28 g). Calorie-dense - realistic plate 1/2 to 2 oz; parmesan as a 1-2 tbsp (5-10 g) finisher.
dairy_cheese_hard.source: FDA RACC cheese 30 g; BDA 30 g (matchbox); USDA string cheese 28 g, deli slice ~19 g, 1 cup shredded 113 g.

low_cal_subgroup._note: Low-cal condiments (hot sauce, mustard, soy, salsa) plate small as flavor, 1-2 tsp typical

sweet_subgroup._note: Honey/maple/jam are calorie-dense sweeteners - plate 1 tsp to 1 tbsp

condiments_sauces.notes: RACC for most dressings/sauces = 2 tbsp (30 g). Snap to tsp/tbsp multiples (5 g steps). Differentiate: high-cal dressings/mayo/sweeteners plate small (1 tsp-1 tbsp); low-cal hot sauce/mustard/soy as a dash (1-2 tsp). Never plate '23 g of ketchup' - snap to 15 g (1 tbsp) or 30 g (2 tbsp).
condiments_sauces.source: FDA RACC dressing/sauce 30 g (2 tbsp); USDA 1 tbsp = 15 g, 1 tbsp honey = 21 g.

global_footgun_rules: WHOLE COUNTABLE foods (eggs, bread slices, tortillas, whole fruit, string cheese, deli slices, medium potato) MUST round to a whole number of units. Plate 2 eggs not 1.6; 2 slices not 2.25; 1 banana not 0.7.
BERRIES ARE SCOOPED BY CUP, never counted by individual berry. '120 g of blueberries' = ~1 cup ~ 80 berries, so never render it as 'N berries'. Same for grapes.
If a single food would need to exceed its max_g to hit a macro target, ADD A SECOND FOOD instead of plating an absurd amount (no '5 tortillas for 1.5 oz turkey', no '300 g of peanut butter').
Calorie-dense foods (oils, nut butter, nuts, cheese, sweeteners) have tight ceilings - if the plan wants more fat, prefer a leaner protein + a normal fat serving over a giant oil pour.
Snap all non-countable grams to the food's scoop_step so portions read as clean numbers a human would actually measure (120 g, not 117.3 g; 1/2 cup, not 0.47 cup).
Cooked grains/legumes: weigh and plate COOKED, in half-cup steps, using the per-grain cup weight (rice 158 g/cup is heavier than pasta 140 g/cup).
